blocks.head: Opportunities identified:
items: Procedures not document or not up to date
Lack of process and tools to support annual procedure review
Lack of control log/database for local procedures management (records of last updates)

blocks.head: Recommended actions:
items: Ensure all customs local procedures are documented and updated as per Global Customs Compliance Policy (Annex I)
Ensure implementation of a control log for local procedure including last update
Ensure most up to date procedures and local control document are uploaded in the Americas Customs Compliance SharePoint Page.
Ensure procedures are updated timely, when required, per regulatory and/or operation changes.

blocks.head: Regional Action Plan
items: Coordinate a full review of country status of documenting procedures to ensure alignment with Policy requirements, mostly with Caribbean CCCL’s.
Provide a template procedures control document for countries.

blocks.head: Opportunities identified:
items: Lack of training plan or materials on customs related requirements and processes
No training records available

blocks.head: Recommended actions:
items: Create a country training plan for customs processes – informal/formal training formats
Track participation and ensure proper record retention.
Utilize root cause analysis of F&P, abandon shipments, and other incidents to identify potential training needs and develop targeted trainings.

blocks.head: Regional Action Plan
items: Collaborate with Global to develop a standard training plan for customs topics.

blocks.head: Best practice identified
items: Cross training between team members would help improve and maximize knowledge in specialized areas (Argentina, Colombia).

blocks.head: Opportunities identified:
items: Individual Customs Compliance Objectives, IKO, not in place for Country Customs Compliance Lead.
Contact details of Country Customs Compliance Lead (CCCL) not provided
Lack of follow up and visibility to SMT/RCCH

blocks.head: Recommended actions:
items: All designated Country Customs Compliance Leads (CCCL) must have at least one IKO related to Customs Compliance.
CCCL's contact information should be shared with SMT timely, for visibility and proper support during Self-Assessment process, corrective action plans implementation, etc.

blocks.head: Regional Action Plan
items: Reinforce responsibilities for CCCL’s roles.

title: Regulatory Supervision – Third Party Brokers Controls (Policy Section 3.5)

blocks.head: Opportunities identified:
items: Broker contracts must be updated with the inclusion of KPIs and SLAs (aligned with the Customs Compliance Policy).

blocks.head: Recommended actions:
items: Periodic evaluations of KPI’s needs to be implemented and monitored.

blocks.head: Regional Action Plan
items: Continue-monitoring of Third-Party documents uploaded in SharePoint, reporting upcoming due dates.
Guide and support the migration process to Shield.

blocks.head: Opportunities identified:
items: Local reconciliation inventory frequency.

blocks.head: Recommended actions:
items: Ensure the process is aligned with the Policy definitions about Inventory control/reconciliation that must be performed at least twice per week)
Define and implement action plans in case of systemic issues identified
Keep updated the procedures related to this topic.

blocks.head: Regional Action Plan
items: Map and support the countries that report F&P for inventory inconsistencies as a root case.

blocks.head: Opportunities identified:
items: Local review process shows that PCM cases are required by cnee (not for DHL’s errors), but number of cases or requestors are not recorded. Sporadic cases.

blocks.head: Recommended actions:
items: Documented procedure must be aligned and updated regularly.
Ensure proper records of PCM requests and define root causes to analyze if PCM could be a compliance risk from Customs perspective.

blocks.head: Regional Action Plan
items: Follow-Up actions if this topic is included into “Show Me The Reds”

blocks.head: Opportunities
items: No effective process executed in place to identify/control unauthorized releases.
No established communication process when the unauthorized release is identified.
No documented procedures aligned to GCCP.

blocks.head: Recommendation:
items: Implement a process to ensure control and proper handling of shipments held by customs or other government agencies.
Develop a reconciliation process to identify and properly handle import shipments that lack a DS, CR event. Verify if they were cleared by customs
Implement a contingency and communication plan when the unauthorized release is identified.
Complete frequent root causes analysis for URL and implement the respective corrective actions.
Perform a GEMBA walk to identify potential risk areas/activities that could lead to unauthorized releases

blocks.head: Regional Action Plan
items: Follow Up URL’s incidences in the region
Provide a regulatory analysis of the impact across the region, including fines and penalties.
Support the implementation of corrective and preventive action plans

blocks.head: Opportunities identified:
items: Local communications related to Customs Compliance information and regulatory changes, are not shared timely

blocks.head: Recommended actions:
items: Ensure proper and timely communication of all relevant regulatory or process changes.

blocks.head: Regional Action Plan
items: No actions needed

title: Regular Customs Declaration Quality Reviews (Policy Section 4.14)

blocks.head: Opportunities identified:
items: Local review process not fully documented and/or implemented to ensure 2% review of formal shipments.
Quality reviews of Low value and other import/export clearance not in place.
Lack of documentation of reviews completed and actions taken.

blocks.head: Recommended actions:
items: Ensure implementation of process to complete quality reviews in alignment with the requirements of the Customs Compliance Policy
Ensure quality reviews are performed for all customs clearance processes. For low value, transit, and others processes the % of shipments reviewed shall be based on local capabilities.
Ensure proper documentation of quality reviews and root cause analysis; Addressing opportunities respectively.

blocks.head: Regional Action Plan
items: Reinforce requirement and support full implementation of Customs Quality Reviews at country level
Collaborate with global to develop a tool to support the country’s documentation of reviews, root cause analysis, and action plans.
